answer: On the tailor's bench lies a pattern book: every coat cut, every fitting, every alteration, dated in the tailor's hand. Proof of tailor certification via master tailors guild reads like that book: a certification the master tailors guild has renewed after every apprenticeship examination. The wharf is the needle: threaded, knotted, and put to cloth. One invented coat needs scissors and nerve. Eighty invented coats need eighty customers, eighty fittings the tailor never held, and the ocean of each is the chalk mark on the sleeve — the zephyr the fitting room, empty at noon.
